overall: The AG found the Saugus School Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by convening at an unlisted location, posting vague March room notices, and holding a January 30 executive session without a proper purpose; January 30 open session minutes were found sufficient.

allegations.summary: Meeting held in a conference room other than the room listed on the January 30 notice, so the procedural steps before executive session were not where the notice said.
allegations.key_passage: Because the January 30 meeting notice inaccurately identified the location where those procedural steps would take place, members of the public were denied this right.

allegations.summary: January 30 notice gave too little detail about the executive session topic (non-unit contract negotiations).
allegations.key_passage: Here, the Committee could not have identified the non-union personnel, because the discussion did not address any individual employees.

allegations.summary: January 30 executive session discussion of non-union contract matters as a general group allegedly lacked a proper executive session purpose.
allegations.key_passage: Accordingly, we conclude that the Committee's January 30 executive session discussion lacked a proper statutory purpose and should have been held in open session.

allegations.summary: March 8, 15, and 22 notices listed only the building address and not the meeting room, which was allegedly too vague about location.
allegations.key_passage: noting that members of the public should not have to guess where in a building a meeting is being held.

allegations.summary: January 30 open session minutes allegedly omitted the meeting location, the chair's pre-executive-session statement, and the executive session purpose.
allegations.key_passage: We therefore conclude that the Committee's January 30 meeting minutes meet the minimum requirements of the Open Meeting Law, though we encourage the Committee to include additional detail in future minutes, including specific meeting room.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
Release the January 30 executive session minutes to the public within thirty (30) days of receipt of the letter, without redaction or withholding under the Public Records Law
remedy_passage: We order the Committee's immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and we caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of intent to violate the law. Furthermore, because a discussion took place during the January 30 executive session that lacked a proper purpose, we order the Committee to release these executive session minutes to the public within thirty (30) days of receipt of this letter.
